name: lsof-deleted-files
title: Identify "Ghost" Deleted Files Holding 100% Disk Space
description: When `df -h` shows 100% full but `du -sh /*` accounts for only 20GB, unlinked files held open by running processes are the culprit.

name: iotop-saturation
title: Isolate Disk I/O Saturation Bottlenecks
description: Detect which exact process and thread is thrashing disk read/write bandwidth and causing high system `iowait`.

name: dmesg-oom-killer
title: Diagnose Out-Of-Memory (OOM) Killer Sacrifices
command: sudo dmesg -T --level=emerg,alert,crit,err | grep -i -E 'oom|killed process|out of memory'
description: Inspect the kernel log ring buffer to determine if the Linux OOM Killer terminated critical services, complete with human-readable timestamps.

name: ss-port-conflict
title: Locate Sockets & Ports Causing Address Conflicts (EADDRINUSE)
description: Pinpoint the exact PID, command name, and user holding a TCP/UDP port preventing your service from binding.

name: ps-zombie-hunt
title: Hunt & Identify Zombie Processes and Their Parents
command: ps -eo stat,ppid,pid,user,comm | awk '$1 ~ /^[Zz]/ {print "Zombie PID: " $3 " | Parent PPID: " $2 " (" $5 ")"}'
description: Locate zombie (`Z`) state processes and reveal the Parent PID (`PPID`) that failed to reap its child via `wait()`.

name: vmstat-triage
title: Diagnose High Load Average: CPU-Bound vs I/O-Blocked
description: Break down high Linux load averages into CPU run-queue saturation versus disk I/O wait blocked threads.

name: find-recent-modified
title: Find All Files Modified in the Last 15 Minutes
description: Track down rogue log writes, malware droppers, or configuration alterations during an active security or operational incident.

name: ps-top-memory
title: List Top 10 Memory Consuming Processes Formatted in MB
description: Generate an accurate, human-readable breakdown of resident memory (RSS) consumed per process.

name: fuser-file-lock
title: Identify Process Holding a File or Port Open with `fuser`
description: Find which process has an active file descriptor or mount lock on a specific file, directory, or socket.

name: strace-relative-latency
title: Trace Relative Syscall Latency on Frozen Processes
description: Measure time elapsed between system calls to identify which kernel syscall is stalling an application.

name: proc-pid-limits
title: Inspect Runtime Resource Limits of a Process
description: Check soft and hard limits for open file descriptors (`Max open files`), memory, and pending signals on a live process.

name: iostat-disk-latency
title: Diagnose Storage Queue Saturation & I/O Latency
description: Measure disk response latency (`await`), queue backlog (`aqu-sz`), and device utilization percentage (`%util`).

name: last-reboot-history
title: Audit System Reboot History & Kernel Crashes
description: Display full calendar timestamps of past system reboots, crashes, and unexpected shutdowns.

name: journalctl-current-errors
title: Query Priority 3 (Errors & Critical) Logs from Current Boot
description: Filter systemd journal strictly to errors, critical alerts, and emergencies from the active boot session.

name: ss-summary
title: High-Level Socket State Distribution & Connection Backlogs
description: Inspect total socket allocation to detect socket leaks, high `TIME-WAIT` pile-ups, or `CLOSE-WAIT` application connection descriptor leaks.

name: curl-timing-waterfall
title: Trace HTTP Latency Waterfall (DNS, TCP, TLS, TTFB)
command:
curl -w "
┌─ Latency Metrics ───────────────────────┐
│ DNS Resolution:     %{time_namelookup}s
│ TCP Handshake:      %{time_connect}s
│ TLS Handshake:      %{time_appconnect}s
│ Pre-transfer Time:  %{time_pretransfer}s
│ Time To First Byte: %{time_starttransfer}s
│ Total Duration:     %{time_total}s
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
" -o /dev/null -s https://api.github.com
description: Dissect the exact microsecond latency timeline of an HTTP request: DNS resolution, TCP handshake, TLS negotiation, Time-To-First-Byte (TTFB), and transfer duration.

name: ip-brief-colored
title: Colored, Brief Interface & IP Assignment Overview
description: Display all local network interfaces, link states (UP/DOWN), and assigned IPv4/IPv6 addresses in clean single-line rows with native ANSI colors.

name: ip-route-destination
title: Determine Outbound Routing Path, Source IP & Next-Hop
description: Determine which local interface, source IP, and gateway the Linux kernel will choose to reach an external destination without generating traffic.

name: tcpdump-web-traffic
title: Sniff HTTP/HTTPS Traffic Without DNS Resolution Lag
command: sudo tcpdump -nn -i any -c 25 'tcp port 80 or tcp port 443'
description: Capture packet headers for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to diagnose dropped SYN packets or connection resets without getting stalled by slow reverse-DNS lookups.

name: mtr-loss-report
title: Diagnose Packet Loss & Jitter with Continuous MTR Report
description: Combines `traceroute` and `ping` into an aggregated statistical report across every network hop to identify ISP or internal routing packet loss.

name: nethogs-bandwidth
title: Monitor Real-Time Bandwidth Consumption by Process
description: Identify the exact running executable and PID saturating server upload or download throughput.

name: bash-tcp-test
title: Pure Bash Remote TCP Port Reachability Check
command: timeout 2 bash -c '</dev/tcp/1.1.1.1/443' && echo "PORT OPEN" || echo "PORT CLOSED"
description: Test if a remote host and TCP port is reachable and accepting connections using pure Bash with zero external dependencies (`nc`, `telnet`, or `nmap` not required).

name: openssl-cert-dates
title: Query Remote TLS / SSL Certificate Expiration Dates
command: echo | openssl s_client -connect github.com:443 -servername github.com 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
description: Extract the exact activation and expiry dates of a remote HTTPS certificate directly from the command line without opening a browser.

name: tcpdump-dns-sniffer
title: Real-Time DNS Query Packet Sniffer
description: Capture outbound and inbound DNS lookup queries on port 53 to diagnose unresolved domain lookups or misconfigured DNS servers.

name: python-http-server
title: Instant Zero-Config HTTP Static File Server
description: Serve the current working directory over local HTTP for rapid file sharing or local web development.

name: resolvectl-flush-cache
title: Flush Local DNS Resolver Cache
description: Force local `systemd-resolved` to purge cached DNS entries and immediately re-query authoritative nameservers.

name: curl-public-ip
title: Query Public IPv4 Address with Zero HTML Bloat
description: Retrieve your public-facing WAN IP address cleanly for automation scripts or CLI inspection.

name: inode-exhaustion-audit
title: Diagnose & Trace Inode Exhaustion
description: When Linux reports `No space left on device` even though `df -h` shows plenty of free gigabytes, the filesystem has run out of available inodes (caused by millions of tiny files or session tokens).

name: find-large-files
title: Sweep the Largest Files Exceeding 500MB
command: sudo find / -xdev -type f -size +500M -exec ls -lh {} + | awk '{print $5, $9}' | sort -hr
description: Rapidly find massive core dumps, runaway log files, or abandoned database snapshots consuming drive capacity.

name: journalctl-vacuum
title: Vacuum Runaway Systemd Journal Logs
description: Reclaim gigabytes of storage occupied by accumulated `systemd-journald` binary logs without rebooting or stopping the logging daemon.

name: lsblk-filesystem-tree
title: Block Device Architecture, Filesystem Types & UUIDs
description: Display an organized ASCII tree of all physical NVMe/SATA drives, partitions, LVM volume groups, and mount points with filesystem formats.

name: dd-disk-benchmark
title: Benchmark True Sequential Storage Write Speed Without Cache
command: dd if=/dev/zero of=./speedtest.tmp bs=1M count=1024 conv=fdatasync status=progress && rm -f ./speedtest.tmp
description: Measure actual raw hardware write throughput by bypassing Linux kernel dirty page writeback buffers.

name: pv-pipe-progress
title: Monitor Data Pipe Progress with Visual Progress Bar (`pv`)
description: Add real-time throughput metrics, elapsed time, total transfer percentage, and ETA to any Unix pipeline.

name: shred-secure-delete
title: Securely Shred & Overwrite Sensitive Files
description: Cryptographically destroy sensitive tokens, SSH private keys, or passwords by overwriting them with random data passes before unlinking.

name: find-empty-files
title: Find and Audit Empty Files & Directories
description: Identify zero-byte files created by failed software builds or stalled application runs.

name: mount-remount-rw
title: Emergency Remount of Read-Only Root Filesystem
description: Recover from filesystem errors that caused the Linux kernel to drop the root partition into read-only mode (`EROFS`).

name: nvme-smart-log
title: Audit NVMe SSD Health & Remaining Wear Life
description: Query the NVMe drive controller for temperature, spare capacity, and percentage of endurance consumed (wear indicator).

name: find-suid-binaries
title: Audit SUID and SGID Executables
description: Detect binaries configured with SUID (`4000`) or SGID (`2000`) permissions that execute with elevated root or group privileges (prime targets for privilege escalation).

name: getcap-binaries
title: Inspect Linux Kernel Capabilities on Binaries
description: Modern Linux splits root privilege into discrete capabilities (`CAP_NET_RAW`, `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, `CAP_SETUID`). Audit which binaries hold elevated capabilities without full root SUID.

name: ssh-failed-logins
title: Track Failed SSH Brute-Force Login Attempts by IP
command: sudo journalctl -u ssh -u sshd -n 2000 --no-pager | grep -i "Failed password" | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i=="from") print $(i+1)}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -15
description: Aggregate failed SSH authentication attempts to identify active IP reconnaissance or brute-force dictionaries.

name: find-world-writable
title: Locate World-Writable Files Outside Safe Temporary Directories
description: Find sensitive configuration or script files accidentally marked world-writable (`chmod 777`), enabling non-privileged users to inject code.

name: chattr-immutable
title: Make Critical Configuration Files Immutable Against Root Deletion
description: Prevent accidental modification or deletion of vital system files (like `/etc/resolv.conf` or `/etc/passwd`) by setting the filesystem immutable flag. Even `root` running `rm -rf` cannot delete or overwrite it.

name: lsattr-inspect
title: Inspect Extended Filesystem Attributes (`lsattr`)
description: Check which files have special kernel filesystem flags set (e.g., `i` immutable, `a` append-only).

name: find-orphaned-files
title: Audit Orphaned Files Belonging to Deleted Users/Groups
description: Locate files whose UID or GID no longer exists in `/etc/passwd` or `/etc/group` (security risk if a new user is assigned that UID).

name: lock-user-account
title: Emergency User Account Lockout & Active Session Termination
command: sudo passwd -l compromised_user && sudo pkill -9 -u compromised_user
description: Instantly lock a compromised user's password and terminate all of their running processes and interactive SSH shells.

name: w-active-users
title: Real-Time Inspection of Logged-In Users & Commands (`w`)
description: View who is currently logged into the system, their originating IP address, idle duration, and the command their terminal is currently executing.

name: log-status-histogram
title: HTTP Status Code Histogram from Web Access Logs
command: awk '{status[$9]++} END {for (code in status) printf "%-6s : %8d requests\n", code, status[code]}' /var/log/nginx/access.log | sort -k 3 -nr
description: Generate an instant frequency distribution and percentage share of HTTP response codes (`200`, `301`, `404`, `500`, `502`) from Nginx or Apache logs.

name: xargs-parallel-execution
title: Multi-Core Parallel Execution with `xargs -P`
description: Accelerate batch operations (e.g., image resizing, compression, hash checks, API pings) by distributing tasks across all available CPU cores.

name: column-table-align
title: Align Jagged Whitespace Data into Clean Terminal Tables
description: Format unaligned delimiter-separated terminal streams or output into neatly aligned columns.

name: jq-nested-filter
title: Slice & Query Complex JSON Streams with `jq`
description: Extract nested keys, filter by condition, and output clean tab-delimited values.

name: urandom-password-gen
title: Generate Cryptographically Secure Passwords from `/dev/urandom`
description: Create a 24-character high-entropy alphanumeric password with special characters without installing third-party utilities.

name: tail-colored-grep
title: Live Log Tail with Real-Time Colorized Keyword Highlighting
description: Follow a streaming log file while highlighting critical error words without buffering delays.

name: comm-process-substitution
title: Find Common Lines Across Two Lists Without Creating Temp Files
description: Compute the exact intersection of two unsorted text files using Bash process substitution.

name: cut-field-slicing
title: Fast Column Slicing from Delimited CSV/TSV Files
description: Extract specific fields rapidly without the overhead of heavy scripting runtimes.

name: renice-priority
title: Dynamically Adjust Process Scheduling Priority (`renice`)
description: Increase or decrease the CPU scheduling priority of a running process without restarting it.

name: taskset-cpu-affinity
title: Pin Process Execution to Specific CPU Cores (`taskset`)
description: Enforce CPU core affinity to prevent context-switching overhead and cache bouncing on multi-core NUMA systems.

name: proc-dirty-memory
title: Inspect Kernel Dirty Memory Pages Waiting on Disk Flush
description: Determine how many megabytes of unwritten memory data are currently backed up in RAM waiting to be committed to disk.

name: pidstat-cpu-breakdown
title: Per-Process CPU Utilization Breakdown with `pidstat`
description: Monitor real-time user-space (`%usr`) vs kernel-space (`%system`) CPU consumption across individual processes.

name: sysctl-reload
title: Apply Linux Kernel Runtime Parameters Without Rebooting
description: Instantly reload sysctl parameters from `/etc/sysctl.conf` into the active Linux kernel.

name: drop-caches-safe
title: Safely Release Inactive Page Cache, Dentries & Inodes
description: Force cached read data and directory structures to be freed from RAM without dropping dirty data.
